title: mission.json (the simulator plan format, D103)
description: D103 (2026-11-15): mission.json is THE plan format the simulator reads; for routes it supersedes the bundle's route.json (route_local.schema.json, kept for v1 readers), while the plan bundle and world pack still give terrain and fields. One mission, built by hand in the web Mission Planer (/mission) or by a live engine job: the user's waypoints with notes, tags and planned stop times, the routed legs between them, the way home, and the planned state over time (O2 used, T_home, O2_home, margin and its binding term). It is the planner's answer to 'what should happen when', so the simulator can compare the live walk with it (deviation in time, O2 and position) without recomputing anything. Self-contained: one file, sent as a download, a POST to a local listener, or a WebGL SendMessage. Same pad-local frame as every bundle file (README 'Coordinate frame'). origin says who computed the numbers: 'mission_planer' = browser estimates on the planner's 5 m routing grid (mission/data.ts), not WS2's validated 3 m engine results; 'computed_live' = a live engine job: legs, path, timeline and summary come from the engine's route (its 3 m routing grid), not the 5 m browser grid, and are still not part of the validated scorecard; 'precomputed' (D110) = the official plan as published in web/public/data (the engine's own route, F9), its numbers copied, not recomputed (tools/make_mission.py --official). origin_label says so on screen. Unknown values are null, never guessed.
x-status: accepted (D103, 2026-11-15): bundle family v1.1.0, additive; v1.1.1 (D110, 2026-11-15, additive): origin also precomputed; schema_version stays 1.1.0; the v1 bundle schemas stay 1.0.0
x-source: origin/waypoint-routing (N0CEO, 36bc6cc) web/src/mission/{plan,router,budget,margin,export}.ts; D103 (computed_live origin, for WP9b); D110 (precomputed origin, for WP9c); config/backend.yaml labels.live and labels.precomputed; contracts/bundle/README.md (frame, plan.schema.json pad/scenario blocks); SPEC F18 alarm rules; config/hud.yaml margin_amber_min

mission_id.description: stable id of this export: 'm-' + first 12 hex of the sha256 of the file with mission_id and created_utc left out, so the same plan always gets the same id

origin.description: 'mission_planer' = built in the browser on the 5 m routing grid; 'computed_live' = built from a live engine job (D40 origin, as plan.json / run_record): the numbers come from the engine's route on its 3 m routing grid, not from the 5 m browser grid; neither is part of the validated scorecard. 'precomputed' (D110) = the official plan's published numbers (web/public/data, the engine's 3 m grid), written by tools/make_mission.py --official

origin_label.description: shown with the mission in the simulator, e.g. 'Mission Planer: browser estimate on the 5 m grid, not part of the validated scorecard' (mission_planer) or config/backend.yaml labels.live 'Computed live · not part of the validated scorecard' (computed_live) or labels.precomputed 'Precomputed · official plan' (precomputed)

planner.description: what built the numbers; the simulator may show it, it does not have to check it

app_commit.description: git commit of the web build

config_hash.description: same rule as plan.json engine.config_hash; null when the web build does not carry it

routing_grid_res_m.description: cell size of the routing grid the legs were found on: the browser grid (5 m) for mission_planer, the engine grid (3 m) for computed_live and precomputed

elevation_res_m.description: resolution of the heights the legs were costed on (mission_planer: fp3d far grid, 8 m; computed_live and precomputed: the engine's terrain)

files.description: data files the numbers came from (mission_planer: mission/data.ts MissionData.files; computed_live: the job's result files; precomputed: the web/public/data files)

frame.description: README 'Coordinate frame': pad-local metres, origin at the pad, x = east, y = north, z = up. Unity position = (x, z, y). A bearing b (deg clockwise from north) is a rotation of b about Unity +y starting from Unity +z.

pad_xy_m.description: pad position in the projection; x_m, y_m = projected - pad_xy_m

pad.description: the rover parking spot the EVA starts and ends at = origin of the frame (same keys as plan.json pad)

elev_m.description: areoid height of the pad, m; z = areoid height - elev_m

scenario.description: physiology variant x suit mass the legs and fields belong to (plan.json scenario)

world.description: terrain to use: the world pack and plan bundle of the same pad and scenario give the fields (t_home, o2_home, home_bearing, pointer) for off-route lookups. null version = not known to the web build; the simulator then uses the pack it has and says so

plan_bundle_id.description: plan.json plan_id of the bundle with this pad and scenario, e.g. 'rank1.nom_104'

constants.description: the budget constants the numbers were computed with (mission/budget.ts BUDGET_CONSTANTS, from config/crew.yaml); copied so the simulator's own O2 model can be checked against the plan

margin_amber_min.description: config/hud.yaml margin_amber_min: SPEC F18 green > this, amber 0..this, red < 0

t_dark_min.description: minutes from EVA start to darkness (clock.json eva.t_dark_min); null = no daylight term

storm_replay.description: D39 storm switch was on when exported: the dose term is in the margin

t_star_min.description: D39: EVA minute the storm tripwire fires (this mission's largest T_home); null when the storm is off

eva_start_utc.description: optional (added 2026-11-15): clock.json eva.start_utc, the EVA start as an instant; the simulator puts its sky there

dose.description: optional (added 2026-11-15): the D39 storm series on the EVA clock (margin.ts doseTimingFromRad at t_star_min), present when storm_replay is true; the simulator adds the dose term tau_dose(t) - T_home and replays the dose rate

series.description: [eva_min, dose rate mGy/h], ascending in eva_min; linear between, clamped outside

waypoints.description: in visit order: pad -> waypoints[0] -> waypoints[1] -> ... -> pad

index.description: 1-based, = the number shown on the map

tags.description: labels only (plan.ts WAYPOINT_TAGS + free tags); they change no number

stop_min.description: planned time at the waypoint, O2 at the station task rate

t_home_min.description: WS2 T_home at the waypoint (the latest it can be left and still be home in time is part of the margin, not this)

legs.description: one per walked segment: 'out' legs pad -> #1 -> ... -> #n, then one 'home' leg #n -> pad along WS2's pointer path (the way the HUD shows home). A leg the router could not find has routed = false and null numbers; the whole mission is then not feasible.

first_row.description: first row of this leg in path.rows

path.description: the planned walk, one row per routing-grid vertex (cell centre), legs in order, each leg starting at its first vertex (a leg's last row and the next leg's first row are the same point). Positions are cell centres, not resampled: the simulator interpolates. t, o2 and the fields are the planner's values at that vertex; between rows they are linear in s. On the 'home' leg t_eva_min = arrival at the last waypoint + its stop + (T_home there - T_home here), o2_used_l likewise with O2_home.

const.s_m: m (horizontal arc length from the leg start)

timeline.description: the planned state over EVA time (mission/margin.ts marginProfile points): what the crew should have used and how much margin they should have at each moment. Values are linear in t between rows. null when a leg is missing or a field value along the route is unknown.

summary.description: the totals the Mission Planer panel shows (mission/budget.ts MissionBudget), null = unknown

feasible.description: every leg routed and timeline.lowest.margin_min >= 0 (and time and O2 margins >= 0); null = not known

label.const: Simulated EVA · real terrain and data
label.description: config/hud.yaml labels.simulated; every simulator view shows it

dummy.description: true when built from web/public/data-dummy; the simulator must show it
